## Why visit

A worthwhile traditional-pub stop in Angel Meadow, where the modest old building sits among a rapidly changing skyline. The attraction is a rotating cask selection, a winter fire and the chance to turn a northern-centre beer walk into a proper pub meal. It fits naturally between the area’s stronger destination pubs without requiring a separate excursion. For experienced beer travellers, its value is the opportunity to investigate unfamiliar regional casks in an everyday freehouse setting; ask what has recently come on rather than expecting a fixed brewery showcase.

## Beer

CAMRA describes six changing cask beers; the operator emphasises regional rotation. The house Fallen Angel bitter’s brewer is not disclosed in the cited listing.

## Cider and perry

**Cider reported; qualification needs checking.** CAMRA mentions two ciders but does not establish their current qualification as real cider. Ask for the producer and product before treating this as a cider destination.

See [how cider is classified](../real-cider.md).

## Food

Seasonal pub dishes and sharing plates, with Sunday roasts. Check the current menu and reserve if the meal is central to your plan.

## Plan the visit

CAMRA’s entry was updated in September 2026. The operator’s food and booking pages disagree about Wednesday kitchen service; confirm directly before relying on a Wednesday meal.

**Getting there:** Combine on foot with Marble Arch, Smithfield Market Tavern and Crown & Kettle; Manchester Victoria and Shudehill are useful approaches.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
